text:
ops-bot: [ALERT] geo-dns-healthcheck: 30% healthcheck failures for service= inference-gw in eu-west1. Several backends marked unhealthy -> DNS fallback to us-east1 triggered. Link: https://pager.redwood/alerts/4321
jamal: saw it, traffic flapped to us-east and we got a spike in cross-region egress + GPU spinups. Any idea why healthchecks started failing?
anya: looks like health probes come from varying SNAT source IPs after the NAT autoscaler changed the SNAT ranges earlier. LB probe source ip mismatch -> backend seen as failing. cc @maria
maria: confirmed. New NAT nodes rolled with different SNAT ranges so the probe source IPs changed mid-check. LB health probe has a whitelist of expected source IPs which doesn't match -> failures.
kevin: quick mitigation idea: set GeoDNS fallback policy to prefer "region-pin" and make fallback strict same-region for 10m while infra stabilizes. Also drop DNS TTL to 15s temporarily. downside: DNS churn + short-term latency variance.
sree: longer-term fix: route healthchecks through reserved egress IPs (we have a small pool of reserved NAT IPs). If we force probes to leave via reserved IPs LB whitelist stays valid. I can implement that in ~20m.
jamal: ops plan suggestion: 1) apply DNS fallback override (prefer same-region) 2) update LB probe whitelist to include new SNAT ranges (or route probes via reserved IP) 3) scale NAT pool to fixed size to avoid autoscaler churn. anyone object?
maria: I'll handle NAT pool + LB probe update. kicking off deploy.
deploy-bot: started job 4321 - job=update-lb-probe-whitelist, initiated by maria.
anya: FYI cost note: the failover created ~6 extra GPU nodes in us-east1 for clients that pin region=nearest, cost estimate ~ $2.4k/hr during the spike. we should add quota guardrail to avoid runaway spins. :exclamation:
kevin: agreed — we need a circuit-breaker for cross-region autoscale. add to backlog after immediate mitigation.
sree: patch ready to route health-checks via reserved-egress-ip (nait-reserved-01). command I used locally: 
```
# force health probe source IP via SNAT pool
gcloud compute routers nats update nat-reserved --nat-external-ip-pool reserved-egress-ips --region eu-west1
```
jamal: sounds good. maria, if you confirm NAT pool scaling done, I'll flip DNS override.
maria: NAT pool scaled to min=3, max=3, autoscaler disabled for now. LB probe whitelist updated to include x.x.200.0/24 and x.x.201.0/24.
jamal: flipping DNS fallback policy now -> TTL 15s, fallback-policy=prefer-same-region for 10m.
ops-bot: [INFO] GeoDNS override applied by jamal at 1772004120.
sree: deploying reserved-egress routing for healthchecks now. will post when done.
deploy-bot: job 4321 completed: update-lb-probe-whitelist -> success (1772004300).
maria: reserved-egress routing done. healthchecks now originate from 35.201.9.12 (reserved). LB no longer rejects probes.
anya: monitoring metrics show traffic shifting back to eu-west1, egress bytes to us-east dropping.
jamal: rolling back DNS override TTL -> 60s in 5m. leaving autoscaler disabled until morning.
kevin: created ticket INFRA-2387 to add cross-region autoscale circuit-breaker + cost alert.
ops-bot: [RESOLVED] geo-dns-healthcheck alert cleared at 1772004865.
maria: postmortem notes: root cause = NAT autoscaler churn + LB whitelist assumptions. action items: 1) reserve healthcheck-egress IPs and document, 2) add autoscaler cooldown for NAT, 3) implement circuit-breaker for cross-region GPU spinups, 4) improve runbook for GeoDNS fallback.
jamal: thanks everyone — good teamwork. :thumbsup:
kevin: small follow-up: please add runbook snippet linking to runbook page and include the gcloud commands used above.
sree: will add to runbook under infra/runbooks/geo-dns-nat.md in the morning.
ops-bot: note: summary posted to #incidents for visibility.
